# ink — terminal markdown reader

## Overview

ink is a feature-rich terminal markdown reader built in Rust. It renders markdown with syntax highlighting, inline images, mermaid diagrams, and more inside an interactive TUI. It ships as a single binary with no runtime dependencies.

## Features

### Rendering
- Full GFM (GitHub Flavored Markdown) support via the comrak parser
- Headings (levels 1-6) with distinct visual styling and block prefixes
- Bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code
- Links with OSC 8 hyperlink support (Cmd+Click / Ctrl+Click in supported terminals)
- Syntax-highlighted code blocks using syntect (supports all major programming languages)
- Tables with auto-sized columns and word wrapping
- Blockquotes with nested support and depth-based coloring
- Ordered and unordered lists with nesting
- Task lists with checkbox rendering
- Footnotes
- Horizontal rules
- Inline/block math ($...$, $$...$$) rendered in code style; :emoji: shortcodes resolved to glyphs
- HTML blocks shown as text; common inline HTML (<br>, <sub>, <sup>, <kbd>) handled rather than dropped
- YAML and TOML frontmatter stripping (optional display)

### Images
- Real pixel rendering via terminal graphics protocols (Kitty graphics, iTerm2 inline, Sixel), auto-detected at startup; --image-protocol auto|kitty|iterm2|sixel|halfblocks
- Falls back to Unicode half-block characters (▄) with 24-bit color on terminals without a graphics protocol (any true-color terminal)
- Images scroll with the document and clip cleanly at the viewport edges
- Loads images from local files (relative paths, contained to the document directory)
- Remote (http/https) images are OFF by default (shown as a placeholder); enable with --remote-images. Even then, private/loopback/link-local/cloud-metadata addresses are blocked, with timeouts and a 20 MB cap
- Decoded images are cached; falls back to emoji placeholder (🖼) if an image can't be loaded or decoded
- Respects --no-images flag

### Mermaid Diagrams
- Renders mermaid code blocks as ASCII art
- Supports flowcharts/graphs, sequence diagrams, pie charts, Gantt charts
- Unknown diagram types get fallback rendering

### Admonitions
- GitHub-style admonition blocks: [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING], [!CAUTION]
- Each type has a distinct color and icon

### Wikilinks
- Converts [[target]] to [target](target.md)
- Converts [[target|display text]] to [display text](target.md)
- Preserves existing file extensions
- Skips wikilinks inside code blocks and inline code

### Interactive TUI
- Built on ratatui with crossterm backend
- Multi-tab: open multiple files, switch with Tab/Shift+Tab
- In-document search with highlighted matches; press Enter then n/N to cycle results, Esc to clear
- Keyboard link opening: press f to label on-screen links, then a letter to open web/mail links or follow a relative .md link
- Help overlay: press ? for a popup of the active keybindings
- Table of contents sidebar showing heading structure, tracks scroll position
- Navigation history with back/forward ([ ] keys or Alt+Arrow)
- Mouse wheel scrolling (can be disabled via behavior.mouse_capture so the terminal handles clicks/selection)
- Event-driven redraw (no CPU when idle) and virtualized rendering for large documents
- Responsive to terminal resizing; shows a message instead of breaking on very small terminals

### File Browser
- Run `ink` with no args (TTY) or `ink .` or `ink <directory>`
- Interactive list of all .md files found recursively
- Filter with /, navigate with j/k/arrows, open with Enter
- Skips hidden files and common non-doc directories (node_modules, target, etc.)
- README files sorted first
- Browser opens a file then exits by default; press Shift+B to reopen, or set behavior.browser_loop = true to return automatically

### Themes
- 8 built-in themes: dark, light, dracula, catppuccin, nord, tokyo-night, gruvbox, solarized
- Auto-detection of terminal background (dark/light)
- Live theme preview with T key; the chosen theme is saved to config
- ink --list-themes lists all available themes (built-in + custom)
- 30+ customizable color properties per theme
- Custom themes via TOML files in ~/.config/ink/themes/
- Honors NO_COLOR and quantizes 24-bit colors to the 256-color palette on non-truecolor terminals

### Other Features
- Presentation mode: split markdown on --- separators with --slides (navigate with arrows/space, slide counter in the status bar)
- Watch mode: auto-reload on file changes with --watch
- Plain output mode: ANSI-colored output without TUI for piping with --plain
- Pager mode: on an interactive terminal, --plain pages long output through $PAGER (default less -R), like bat; --no-pager disables it
- Document outline: `ink outline <file>` shows heading structure
- Document stats: `ink stats <file>` shows word count, reading time, element counts
- Markdown diff: `ink diff <file_a> <file_b>` compares two files with a real Myers line diff
- Shell integration: `ink shell-setup bash|zsh|fish` prints config snippets
- Shell completions: `ink completions bash|zsh|fish|powershell|elvish`
- Man page: `ink man` (troff)
- URL fetching: open markdown from HTTP/HTTPS URLs directly (timeout- and size-capped)
- Stdin support: pipe markdown content to ink

### Security
- Strips terminal control/escape bytes (ESC, C0, C1, DEL) from all rendered text, covering both the TUI and --plain, preventing ANSI/OSC escape-sequence and hyperlink injection from untrusted markdown
- Link destinations are scheme-validated (http/https/mailto/relative only); javascript:, file:, data: and control-byte URLs are dropped
- Remote images off by default; SSRF protections when enabled (see Images)
- Relative file/image paths are canonicalized and contained to the document's directory; absolute paths rejected
- install.sh verifies a published SHA256SUMS manifest before installing; CI runs cargo audit

### Keybindings
- j/k/↑/↓: scroll up/down
- Space/PageDown: page down
- PageUp: page up
- G/End: jump to end
- Home: jump to start
- Ctrl+f/Ctrl+b: page down/up
- Ctrl+d/Ctrl+u: half-page down/up
- n/N: next/previous heading (cycles search matches after a search)
- /: search
- f: link-hint mode (open/follow links by letter)
- ?: help overlay
- t: toggle table of contents
- T: theme picker (saved to config)
- Enter: follow first visible link
- [/]: navigation back/forward
- Tab/Shift+Tab: next/previous tab
- Shift+B: reopen file browser
- q/Esc/Ctrl+C: quit (first press clears an active search)
- Presets: default (vim-flavored), vim, emacs; fully customizable, two-key chords supported

## Configuration

Config file: ~/.config/ink/config.toml

```toml
theme = "catppuccin"
width = 90
spacing = "normal"
toc = false
frontmatter = false

[behavior]
browser_loop = false   # return to browser after closing a doc
mouse_capture = true    # set false to let the terminal handle clicks/selection

[keybindings]
preset = "emacs"        # default | vim | emacs
```

## Technical Stack
- Language: Rust
- Markdown parser: comrak (GFM-compliant)
- TUI framework: ratatui + crossterm
- Syntax highlighting: syntect
- Image decoding: image crate
- CLI: clap
- License: Free to use, cannot be sold (see LICENSE)
